change.title: pr-10
change.description: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding
change.author: Robin Ward

findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset or doesn't match a category
findings.body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the join returns a row. A site_settings row exists only when an admin has changed the setting from its default (`embed_category: ''`, removed from config/site_settings.yml). The join also needs the value to match a category name exactly. In every other case the result is empty, and `[0]` raises (PG::Result IndexError, or nil['id']). The `category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 never runs, so the migration aborts on most installs. The same pattern on line 15 also fails if `uncategorized_category_id` has no row. Check `cmd_tuples`/`ntuples` before indexing, as line 19 already does.

findings.title: Migrated hosts keep their scheme/path, so existing embeds stop working
findings.body: The old `allows_embeddable_host?` normalised each entry with `URI(h).host` (removed lines in app/models/site_setting.rb), so values like `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234` worked. The removed specs tested exactly those values. The migration inserts each raw line with SQL and skips the model's `before_validation` stripping (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8). `record_for_host` then compares `lower(host)` with the bare `uri.host` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17), so these sites start getting 'invalid referer host' after upgrading and nothing tells them why. Blank lines and trailing `\r` are also inserted unchanged. Strip the scheme, path and whitespace, and skip empty entries, before inserting.

findings.title: before_validation raises on a nil host
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil. `save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without checking it (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23), so a create or update request without a host returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?` or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

findings.title: Validation accepts hosts that can never match, and rejects some the old setting allowed
findings.body: The regex allows `:port`. `record_for_host` compares with `uri.host`, which never includes a port, so `example.com:8080` saves but never matches. The `[a-z]{2,5}` TLD rule rejects `localhost` and longer TLDs. There is also no uniqueness validation, so duplicate hosts can be added.

findings.title: New host saved without a category shows no category badge
findings.body: For a new host, `categoryId` starts as null (line 9), and `edit()`, which would set it, never runs. If the admin doesn't pick a category, the server stores `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25). The client still sets `category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)`, so the row shows an empty badge until the page is reloaded. Use the `category_id` from the save response instead of the local `categoryId`.

findings.title: Delete failure is silent
findings.body: `destroyRecord()` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, unlike `save` on line 40. If the request fails, the row stays and the admin gets no message.

findings.title: Unknown id gives a 500 instead of a 404
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first` returns nil for an unknown id, and `host.destroy` (and `save_host` on line 11) then raise NoMethodError. Use `find` / `find_by!` or raise `Discourse::NotFound`.

findings.title: saveChanges and the PUT customize/embedding endpoint are dead
findings.body: No template calls `saveChanges`. `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9) doesn't change anything; it only re-renders. Remove both, or implement them.

findings.title: `hydrated || []` is dead and missing ids become undefined entries
findings.body: `Array#map` always returns an array, so the `|| []` never applies. `obj[k]` is also not checked: if it is null, `.map` throws. Ids that `_lookupSubType` can't resolve become `undefined` entries in the array. Filter them out.

findings.title: `replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore
findings.body: A type with two underscores (for example `site_customization_x`) won't be normalised. Use `/_/g`.

findings.title: Test named 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests that
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer depends on embeddable hosts. This example passes only because `embed_truncate` is false by default and the built topic has no embed. Rename or remove it. The `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the nested `before` (line 1409) is likewise irrelevant.

findings.title: `find('fruit', 2)` actually gets apple
findings.body: The pretender's `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]` (test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6:227). The test passes only because of that. Banana's `color_ids` is `[3]`, so the assertions of ids 1 and 2 contradict the id the test asks for. Use id 1, or make the pretender honour `:id`.

findings.title: Fabricator files have swapped contents
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now holds the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds all the category fabricators. It works, but anyone looking for either fabricator will look in the wrong file. Swap them back.

findings.title: No coverage for create/update/destroy
findings.body: The specs only check the class hierarchy. The nil-host and unknown-id failures above would show up in a spec for each action.

contracts.action: Migration deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings after copying them
contracts.equivalent_path: Old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? read embeddable_hosts with URI normalisation
contracts.before_after: Before: hosts were matched after normalising with URI(h).host. After: raw lines are copied without normalisation, then the source rows are deleted
contracts.visible_effect: Hosts saved with a scheme or path no longer match a referer, so embeds fail with 'invalid referer host'
contracts.failure_mode: The DELETE runs in the same migration, so the original values are lost and can't be re-derived once copied in un-normalised form. On sites without embed_category the migration raises at line 11 before reaching the DELETE

contracts.before_after: New feature. Deletes by id after a bootbox confirm
contracts.visible_effect: On success the row is removed through deleteHost
contracts.failure_mode: No catch, so a failed request leaves the row with no message. A server call with an unknown id hits nil.destroy and returns a 500

contracts.action: Admin adds or saves a host
contracts.before_after: Server falls back to the uncategorized category when category_id is blank; the client uses its local categoryId
contracts.visible_effect: A new host saved without a category shows an empty badge until reload
contracts.failure_mode: Save errors appear through popupAjaxError. A nil host makes before_validation raise, returning a 500

contracts.action: Embedded topic import picks its category from the matching EmbeddableHost
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously SiteSetting.embed_category (a category name) passed to PostCreator
contracts.before_after: Now passes an integer category id, or nil when no host matches (for example feed polling from an unlisted host), which falls back to the default category
contracts.visible_effect: The topic is created in the host's category

summary: This PR moves the embeddable hosts setting into a new embeddable_hosts table, adds an admin screen to manage it, and lets each host set the category its embedded topics go to. The migration has two serious problems. First, it crashes on any site where embed_category was never set or doesn't match a category name (blocker). Second, it copies host values without stripping the scheme or path, so sites with values like `http://host` lose embedding silently after upgrading (fix). Smaller issues: the model's before_validation raises on a nil host; a new host saved without a category shows no badge until reload; deletes fail silently; and unknown ids return a 500. Some tests and fabricator files are misleading, and the controller specs only check the class hierarchy.
